chunks: God presents the example of a town which enjoyed peace and security, its provisions coming from everywhere in abundance, but it denied the favours of God; so God acquainted it with intimate hunger and fear (as punishment) for what they had done.
ai.seo_question: What is the parable of the secure town in Surah An-Nahl and what does it teach about gratitude?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse (16:112) is often interpreted as referring to the pre-Islamic town of Mecca or the Banu Qurayza, highlighting how material security can lead to spiritual arrogance if gratitude (shukr) is neglected. The 'garment' of hunger and fear symbolizes the enveloping nature of divine retribution, serving as a cautionary tale for the faithful to maintain humility amidst prosperity.
